clue.text: Generous applause? A bit

parts.note: to give someone a hand is to applaud them
a bit of something is some of it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether clapping counts as being generous, and is told it does, a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome gift or sum is a large, liberal one, so the adjective can mean open-handed.

clue.text: Success, covering top of lift shaft

indicators.note: the word for success wraps round and so covers the letter taken from lift

parts.note: a hit is a success, like a hit record

indicators.note: top of picks the opening letter of the word lift in a down clue

explanation.surface: A building report: the lift shaft is a triumph, with something covering its top.
explanation.definitionFit: The handle of a sword or dagger, its grip end, can be called its shaft in a loose sense.

clue.text: Viciously attack note on instrument

parts.note: a uke is a ukulele, a small guitar-like instrument

explanation.surface: A violent assault on a musical note played on some instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To bomb with nuclear weapons, and informally to destroy or attack savagely.

clue.text: Soviet leader chucked in a German camp

indicators.note: chucked means thrown away, so the word in is discarded from the leader's name

parts.note: Joseph Stalin led the Soviet Union

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader thrown into a German prison camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chucked in' reads as one phrase but 'in' is the very word removed from STALIN, leaving STAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War.

clue.text: Leading pair in heretic group of mine almost converted Diana

parts.note: belonging to me is my
Jan Hus was a Bohemian reformer burned as a heretic
a band is a group, as of musicians

indicators.note: converted means changed into a new form, so the shortened name is rearranged
almost means the name Diana loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Reads as a church story: a heretical sect led by two people converts a woman called Diana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts DIANA to DIAN, which 'converted' rearranges to ANDI. The answer is Queen Elizabeth II's famous phrase about herself and Prince Philip.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was the Queen's habitual way of naming herself and her consort, the realm's foremost couple.

clue.text: Agree with right-wing scoundrel

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the British right-wing party
a cur is a contemptible man, a cad

explanation.surface: Siding with a rogue from the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion, a straight synonym of agree.

clue.text: Soldiers move gleefully, clutching new weaponry

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the dancing word holds the letter for new

parts.note: to dance is to move with joy

explanation.surface: Troops jig happily while gripping brand-new arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means military supplies, especially artillery and munitions.

clue.text: Appeal Lily put out to Doris: stop work

indicators.note: put out to means a letter is sent away from the flower's name over to the actress's surname

parts.note: the calla is the arum lily
it is sex appeal, as in the it girl
Doris Day was an American singer and actress

explanation.surface: Lily makes an appeal to her friend Doris, telling her to knock off.
explanation.walkthrough: Lily is not a woman but the calla lily; 'put out to' sends that flower's last letter over to the actress's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To call it a day is the idiom for ending one's work for the time being.

clue.text: Bank stores finished letter with agreement but no will

indicators.note: stores means keeps inside, so the word for bank holds the other piece

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a finished letter has been signed off

explanation.surface: A bank keeps a completed letter of consent but no testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' looks like a legal testament to match the bank, but it means willingness.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting this way means accepting something unwillingly, going along without wanting to.

clue.text: Show appreciation of the hard stuff without hesitation

definitions.text: Show appreciation of the hard stuff
definitions.meaning: read literally, to enjoy a measure of spirits
an idiom meaning instantly and eagerly

explanation.surface: Someone who enjoys strong liquor and would accept a drink instantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very quickly and eagerly, with no pause for thought.

clue.text: Backs small numbers to receive mercy

indicators.note: to receive means to take in, so the numbers take in the word for mercy

parts.note: threes are small numbers
to give no quarter is to show no mercy

explanation.surface: Supporters back modest figures so that some clemency is shown.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the backs include the four three-quarters, so the plural noun matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby union's three-quarter backs are wings and centres, part of the back line.

clue.text: Island of the Greeks, or of the Spanish

definitions.meaning: an Aegean island in the Cyclades, birthplace of Apollo in myth
... is Spanish for of the, before a masculine plural

explanation.surface: Asking whether an island belongs to Greece or to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cycladic island sacred to Apollo and Artemis, and also the Spanish phrase for of the.

clue.text: Orienteering involves partners in selfish behaviour

indicators.note: involves means includes, so the orienteering skill takes in the partners

parts.note: orienteering is navigation by map reading
N and S, north and south, are partners at bridge

explanation.surface: A sport where couples behave thoughtlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with legs wide apart on public transport, taking more than one's share of seats, is a selfish habit.

clue.text: Drinking tea, endlessly observing Albert

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the shortened word holds the tea
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: observing is watching
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Someone sipping tea while keeping a constant eye on a man named Albert.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert is not a man but an Albert chain, named after Prince Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: An Albert is a heavy chain for a pocket watch, named after Queen Victoria's consort.

clue.text: theguardian.com is one no man made work

definitions.note: the address is an example of the noun, an internet address

indicators.note: work as a verb means to shape or knead, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boast that the newspaper's website is a creation no human produced.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet address like this identifies a website, so it is an example of the term.

clue.text: Hello, sailor!

parts.note: the cry a sailor uses to hail another ship, read as a greeting from a seaman rather than the cheeky catchphrase

explanation.surface: The cheeky catchphrase used to greet a passing seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical call used to hail a ship or attract attention, the seafarer's greeting.

clue.text: Altering a single letter, strong grip secretary's taken on bureaucratic nightmare

indicators.note: altering one letter means one letter of the joined words is swapped for another
taken on means the grip word goes on after the secretary

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
purchase is a firm hold or grip

explanation.surface: An office tale: a secretary's firm hold tangled in red tape, with one letter changed.
explanation.walkthrough: PA plus PURCHASE gives PAPURCHASE; the U becomes E.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless form-filling and document shuffling is called this, after the cross-country game of following a paper trail.

clue.text: Delight to beat American singing group

parts.note: glee is delight
to club is to beat with a stick

explanation.surface: Delighted to defeat a US choir.
explanation.definitionFit: In American schools and colleges, a choir that sings short songs is called by this name.

clue.text: Water could flow and came thus from woodwork?

indicators.note: flow suggests liquid letters running freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Water seeping out of wooden panelling, as if it emerged that way.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is coming out of the woodwork: appearing unexpectedly, often unwelcome, like insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatures emerging from woodwork creep out slowly on hands and knees, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Lament singular country expressed?

indicators.note: singular means the plural ending S is dropped
expressed means spoken, so the country is pronounced not spelt

parts.note: Wales is a country of the UK, and it is pronounced like the word wails

explanation.surface: Grieving for a particular nation, put into words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressed' turns WALES into its sound-alike WAILS; 'singular' drops the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To wail is to cry out in grief, a synonym of mourn.

clue.text: Not good to throw around gold coin

indicators.note: around means the shortened throw word goes round the gold
not good means the letter G, for good, is removed

parts.note: to fling is to throw
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: It is bad form to toss a gold coin about.
explanation.definitionFit: An old British coin worth two shillings, originally a gold coin of Florence.

clue.text: Run into tax on business producing hypocritical poster

indicators.note: on means the business comes first in the across answer, with the rest on it

parts.note: a concern is a business

indicators.note: into means the run is placed inside the tax

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A firm crashes into a levy and ends up with someone two-faced on the posters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' is not a placard but someone who posts online.
explanation.definitionFit: An online commenter who feigns sympathy while really undermining a cause is a hypocritical poster.

clue.text: Using loose pad, I dry bed

parts.note: a wad is a pad of loose soft material

explanation.surface: Someone lies on a slack mattress pad to keep the bed dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert watercourse that is dry except in the rainy season, a dry riverbed.

clue.text: Agog to see Wounded Knee

indicators.note: wounded means damaged, so the letters are hurt into a new order

explanation.surface: Eager to visit Wounded Knee, the South Dakota massacre site.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agog is being eager and excited, so it means very enthusiastic.

clue.text: A disguise said to be useful

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a veil is something that disguises

explanation.surface: A mask, it is claimed, comes in handy.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to help or be of use, as in to no avail.

clue.text: Drunk, be taken over by hopeless inertia

indicators.note: hopeless means a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drinker overcome by helpless sluggishness.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate person is intoxicated, so the adjective means drunk.

clue.text: It's unavoidable when born a dame

definitions.note: a clause meaning at a time when it is necessary

parts.note: nee means born, used before a maiden name
DBE, Dame Commander of the British Empire, is the honour that makes a woman a dame

explanation.surface: Destiny says being born a dame is inevitable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, as in if need be, means if it is necessary, when there is no avoiding it.

clue.text: A descendant tours one foreign capital

indicators.note: tours means travels round, so the descendant goes around the other piece

parts.note: a scion is a descendant
un is French for one

explanation.surface: An heir travelling around a foreign capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Asuncion is the capital city of Paraguay.
